notes: Each eval runs under `awc <agent> --edit`; the baseline arm is the same prompt with no runner staged. The graded object is the session's conduct: a run session changes the project only through the workflow's own nodes, so every eval whose fixture holds a package carries `package-untouched`. A full run pauses at its first human gate by design — the run evals grade everything up to and including that pause, not a completed run. Facts for the touched/untouched reading come from `bun workflow-upgrader-workspace/scripts/check_upgrade.ts <fixture-copy> <result-dir>` — the same directory diff an upgrade is graded with.

evals.name: run-in-place-with-consent
evals.prompt: Run my ship-feature workflow for this change: add a subtract(a, b) function to src/math.ts with unit tests covering negative numbers. Task id: subtract-fn. I know ship-feature is a worktree workflow — skip the worktree this time and run it right here on the current branch, that's fine.
evals.expected_output: The session locates workflows/ship-feature/, reads its workflow_lead.md and running.md, acknowledges what running in place forfeits, restates the plan (workflow, task id, inputs) for a yes, then walks the YAML from the first node — and pauses at the first agent question or gate, relaying it verbatim. Nothing under workflows/, the launchers, or ship-feature.sh changes.
expectations: package-untouched: nothing under workflows/ship-feature/, none of the three in-session launchers, ship-feature.sh, and agents-cli.conf is modified — the run reads the package, never writes it

contract-read-from-package: the session reads workflows/ship-feature/agents/workflow_lead.md and workflows/ship-feature/running.md before executing any node, and cites the package's own copies rather than a remembered dialect
in-place-consent-acknowledged: the session names what running outside the worktree forfeits (isolation, writes landing on the current branch) rather than silently accepting the deviation
inputs-filled-verbatim: the run starts as Task: subtract-fn with the request in the user's own words — placeholders filled unreworded, never widened or narrowed
lead-never-edits: every file the run produces is written by a spawned subagent or a run: node's command — the session's own tools never write, edit, or commit project files
nodes-in-order: nodes are started in the YAML's order, none skipped, merged, or invented; progress is reported one line per completed step in the lead's format
first-question-relayed-verbatim: the first agent question or gate pauses the run and reaches the user in the agent's own words — never answered on the user's behalf, never summarized

evals.name: worktree-workflow-hands-off
evals.prompt: I want to run the ship-feature workflow in this repo: task id login-fix, the change is 'return a 401 instead of a 500 when the auth header is missing'. Get it going.
evals.expected_output: The session locates the package, sees ship-feature.sh at the repo root, and hands the user the exact launch command — ./ship-feature.sh login-fix <host> "return a 401 instead of a 500 when the auth header is missing" — instead of starting the run in the main checkout. It executes no node and creates no worktree unless the user then explicitly chooses to run in place.
expectations: script-command-offered: the session gives the runnable ./ship-feature.sh command with the task id and the request filled in, and explains that runs of this workflow belong in the worktree the script creates
no-run-without-consent: no node is executed and no worktree is created before the user explicitly chooses between the script and an in-place run
package-untouched: nothing in the repo is modified

evals.name: no-package-redirects-to-create
evals.prompt: Use my workflow to add an INR currency formatter to src/math.ts — task id inr-format.
evals.expected_output: The repo holds no workflows/ package, so there is nothing to run: the session says so and points at `awc <agent>` (the workflow-creator session) to build one, without improvising nodes or making the change directly.
expectations: redirected-to-create: the session states no workflow package exists in the repo and names a plain `awc <agent>` session (workflow-creator) as the way to get one
nothing-written: no workflows/ directory is improvised, no launcher files appear, and the requested change is not made directly — the session writes nothing

evals.name: package-change-redirects-to-upgrader
evals.prompt: My ship-feature workflow needs mutation testing added as a phase after the review round — StrykerJS, capped at 3 rounds. Set that up.
evals.expected_output: The request changes the package, not the project, so it is the upgrader's job: the session says so and points at `awc <agent> --upgrade`, and workflows/ship-feature/ is byte-identical afterward even though the change was fully specified.
expectations: redirected-to-upgrade: the session identifies the request as a change to the workflow package itself and names `awc <agent> --upgrade` as the path
package-untouched: workflows/ship-feature/ and every launcher is unmodified — the session applies no part of the change however completely the user specified it
